title: Database credentials hardcoded in the source
description: The connection string with the admin password is a constant in the code.

title: API key hardcoded in the source
description: The API key is a constant in the code instead of configuration or a secret store.

title: A connection opened in the constructor is never closed
description: The service opens a SqlConnection for its whole life, does not implement IDisposable and never disposes it.

title: SQL injection through tableName and userId
description: Both values are interpolated into the SQL text.

title: Obsolete DES encryption
description: DES has a 56-bit key and is broken; use AES-GCM or another modern authenticated cipher.

title: Hardcoded encryption key and IV
description: A constant key and a fixed IV make the ciphertext easy to decrypt and identical for identical data.

title: Path traversal in ReadUserFileAsync
description: fileName is put into the path unchecked, so ..\ sequences read files outside the folder.

title: Command injection
description: The caller's text is executed by cmd.exe.

title: Cross-site scripting through the comment
description: The comment is put into HTML without encoding and returned to the browser.

title: Passwords are stored and compared in plain text
description: The query compares the password column directly, so passwords are stored unhashed.

title: The connection string is put into an exception message
description: The failed-login exception carries the connection string with its password.

title: The API key is returned to the caller
description: Every successful login hands out the service's own API key.

title: Database errors expose the connection string and schema
description: The rethrown exception carries the connection string and table name and drops the original exception.

title: Non-atomic increment of a shared counter
description: Concurrent calls can return the same id; use Interlocked.Increment.

title: Disposable objects created in a loop and never disposed
description: A million iterations each create a FileStream, MemoryStream and HttpClient without disposing them, leaking file handles and sockets.

title: Security tokens from a fixed-seed Random
description: Random with a constant seed produces the same token every time; use RandomNumberGenerator.
